scan_classes.why: a named third-party business or private individual — not the publisher's to give away

scan_classes.name: account_identity
scan_classes.why: identifiers that resolve to one live account on the vendor's side

scan_classes.name: machine_identity
scan_classes.why: a machine id assigned a literal value — pins the export to one physical desktop

scan_classes.name: home_path
scan_classes.why: a local absolute path — leaks the machine layout and the operator's username

scan_classes.name: credential_shape
scan_classes.why: a credential-shaped literal: a key prefix, a PEM header, or a secret-named assignment

scan_pattern_disclosure: digests only — two of these patterns are themselves the identity strings being refused, so publishing them would undo the export

optional_dependencies.why: bin/gb-pull-inventory.py decrypts the desktop's own safeStorage v10 blob to read the local inventory replica. AES-CBC is not in the standard library, the import sits inside `decrypt()`, and every other verb in the tool runs without it.

checks: refusal scan over every exported text line (5 classes, all hits reported)
self-sufficiency: every internal import is present in the export
stdlib purity: every other import resolves to this interpreter's stdlib, except a declared optional extra, which must additionally be imported lazily
version agreement across bin/gb, pyproject.toml, grok_bot_ops/__init__.py
self_digest: absent — this file is what the other digests are recorded in
